meta.source: nb_gene_density (log1p count of annotated genes within +-1 Mb of gene start, genome_wide.coords(), autosomes only, n=18916) rigidly CIRCULARLY SHIFTED by a pre-registered offset along the global (chromosome, start) gene order. Offsets: 20 drawn from seed 20260720 in [500, n-500]; the registered slot runs the most-decorrelated one. Marginal distribution and autocorrelation function are preserved EXACTLY; the gene->chromosome map is untouched, so group_by='chromosome' scoring is identical to the true label's. labels_for_offset(D, resid=True) gives the matching control for nb_gene_density_resid; shift_diagnostics() reports rho(true, shifted) for the full 20-shift distribution.
meta.unfair_reason: None declared, and none is defensible. A circularly shifted density field is derived from no expression panel and carries no residue information, so coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562 and esm2 are all fair and all must be run. In particular coexpr_k562's CNV/dosage channel is NOT grounds for exclusion here (unlike h_chromosome/h_position): the shifted label is not chromosome identity and copy-number dosage supplies no information about a rotated within-chromosome field. Declaring any ref unfair on this row would be the selective-baseline trap applied to the one row whose baseline margins are meaningless anyway.
meta.expect: GATE-BLOCKER, subtractive by design — this row is not a candidate discovery and must never be promoted to the ATLAS as a passer. Prediction under the artefact hypothesis: HIGH z (the model encodes position, and the permutation null cannot reject a smooth-in-position label) and a LARGE positive margin over all four references (none of them can express a coordinate-space rotation at all), i.e. a spurious 'decodable + model_specific' verdict. THE BASELINE MARGINS ON THIS ROW ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING — the decisive comparison is against nb_gene_density's OWN score on the identical 18916-gene set, identical folds, identical metric, plus the LSA top-K co-occurrence basis for slate consistency. Pre-registered rule: shifted within MIN_MARGIN (0.02) of true -> RETRACT nb_gene_density and nb_gene_density_resid as smoothness artefacts before any Stage-2 steering spend. Shifted ~0 with true intact -> the permutation null is exonerated for the genome-architecture family and nb_gene_density earns its steering test (push the top-decile-density direction at one gene block, read next-gene logits at a disjoint block ON A DIFFERENT CHROMOSOME so the effect cannot be a positional restatement, norm-matched random control, monotone alpha dose-response).

meta.source: sd of standardised mean-expression rank across 3 RANDOM DISJOINT CELL-THIRDS of the fetal-gut panel (coexpr_devel, 8000 cells, rng seed 0), duplicate symbols collapsed by keeping the higher-expressed row exactly as h_context_lability does, ranked within the IDENTICAL devel/k562/hsc symbol intersection (n=4790) so the margin is directly comparable to context_lability's. Same tissue, same assay, same cells' biology in all three thirds — every difference between them is sampling noise.
meta.expect: SUBTRACTIVE NULL for context_lability, and the decisive input to the program's next spend. Read the model-minus-coexpr(TS) margin, NOT margin_over_refs. (a) If this pseudo-label's model-minus-coexpr(TS) margin approaches context_lability's +0.108, context_lability is RETRACTED — the margin is rank-instability-of-low-count-genes, reproducible with zero biology — and Stage 2 is not spent on it. (b) If this margin is near zero while the real label holds +0.108, context_lability is CLEARED of the sampling-noise alternative and goes straight to the steering harness (push the high-lability direction at one gene block, read MaxToki's next-gene logits at a disjoint block, norm-matched random control, monotone alpha dose-response, effect quoted against the substitution ceiling). EXPECTED ON THE OTHER BASES: coexpr_devel should WIN OUTRIGHT — the label comes from that panel's own cells — so margin_over_refs and margin_all_refs will both be strongly negative and 'not model specific' is the correct and uninformative screen verdict for this row. That negative margin is the calibration; a coexpr_devel loss would mean the co-expression arm is broken. esm2 should be at chance: protein sequence cannot encode which cells landed in which random third.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE DECLARED, deliberately, and the omission is the methodological point. A valid mechanism IS available for coexpr_devel — the label is computed from that panel's own cells, so it is an own-panel reference in exactly the sense h_chromosome's K562 exclusion was about — and excluding it would raise this null's headline margin. Declaring it unfair would break SYMMETRY with context_lability, whose own label also draws on the devel panel and which is screened with all four references live. A null that gets a concession its target did not get is not a null. So: all four references are reported, none is gated out, and the head-to-head statistic quoted against context_lability is MODEL MINUS COEXPR(TABULA SAPIENS), because TS is a NON-SOURCE panel for the real label and for the pseudo label alike — the only reference that is symmetric between them.
meta.headline_stat: model_best - coexpr   (Tabula Sapiens; the only reference that is non-source for BOTH the real context_lability label and this pseudo label)

meta.source: signed local gene-density asymmetry from UCE species_chrom coordinates: for each autosomal gene at coordinate-sorted index i, a_i = log1p(#genes in (start, start+1Mb]) - log1p(#genes in [start-1Mb, start)), then least-squares residualised WITHIN CHROMOSOME on [vander(position_rank, 6), vander(density_rank, 4)[:, :3]]. n=18916; raw a mean 0.000 sd 0.817; residual sd 0.789.
meta.scoring_note: THE LABEL IS SIGNED (antisymmetric under chromosome reflection). screen.py:57 and :60 take abs() of the per-chromosome Spearman rho. That must NOT be applied here: a probe predicting the reversed sign would score as perfect, and abs() lifts the permutation null asymmetrically, distorting z. Score with SIGNED within-chromosome rho averaged with sign preserved, and build the null the identical way. If the runner cannot honour this, treat the emitted score and z as UNINTERPRETABLE rather than reporting them.
meta.fair_refs_note: All four screen references are fair and none is excluded. The competitor this label actually needs is one screen.py does not yet carry: a POSITION-PLUS-DENSITY ORACLE — the same RidgeCV probe fed only [within-chromosome position rank, its polynomial expansion, the 1-Mb density level]. For any genome-structure label that oracle, not co-expression, is the real baseline, and no existing screen row has faced it. The STRONG LSA top-K shallow co-occurrence basis (shallow_coocc_baseline.py) is likewise a fair and stronger co-occurrence competitor than screen.py's weak coexpr. Both are requested as additions, not exclusions.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE — deliberately empty, including coexpr_k562, which the sibling chromosome and position hypotheses do exclude. Their reason is copy-number dosage: in an aneuploid line a whole segment is amplified, so same-segment genes co-vary and CHROMOSOME identity leaks through DNA dosage. That mechanism is SYMMETRIC within a segment — a uniform gain over a multi-megabase block adds the same dosage to the 1-Mb flank upstream and downstream of a gene, and cannot manufacture an ANTISYMMETRIC local quantity except within one window of a segment breakpoint. So the k562 excuse does not transfer, and k562 stays in the gate: a k562 win here would be a RED FLAG about the label construction (a leak we have not identified), not a nuisance to excuse.
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, and informative in both directions — this is a strictly harder ask than the density family. If it passes, the model carries a DIRECTIONAL genome-architecture channel that no smooth positional code can produce, and it is the batch's best Gate-3 candidate because a signed label licenses a signed dose-response. If it fails while raw density passes, the model has neighbourhood MAGNITUDE only and the directional claim is cleanly refuted. The near-zero raw dependence on position (0.055 mean |rho|) means a null result here cannot be blamed on over-residualisation.

meta.source: Hierarchy height h=(out-in)/(out+in) on the TF->TF subgraph of [DoRothEA A/B/C UNION TRRUST] (|E|=37,232 edges, 917 TFs, 5,172 TF->TF edges, 601 TFs with >=3 TF->TF edges get an h). Label(non-TF gene) = mean h over its >=3 regulators that carry an h; n=3,207 labelled, 3,117 overlap the coexpr panel, 1,106 survive the 6-basis intersection. Residualised on [log1p(in-degree in E), TS panel breadth, TS log mean abundance], linear + quadratic. DoRothEA tier D is EXCLUDED (244,276 of 276,548 edges; inferred from bulk co-expression).
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, leaning FAIL but asymmetric — only a MODEL win is interpretable. The argument FOR: cascade depth is antisymmetric (an out-minus-in difference) while co-expression is symmetric, so `coexpr` has no direct channel to it, and the D tier that would have supplied one is excluded. The argument AGAINST: high-h master regulators (E2F/ETS/EGR/STAT families) drive broad housekeeping programmes and low-h sink TFs drive tissue-restricted ones, so depth may be a laundered expression-breadth label — which is exactly what the breadth+abundance residualisation is there to strip. A coexpr win is therefore uninformative (it retains the full profile and can rebuild breadth), whereas a maxtoki win over all four fair refs would say the gene table encodes cascade ORDER, not merely co-regulation.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE DECLARED — all four screen references (coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562, esm2) are FAIR here and the margin is gated on all of them. Stated explicitly because the chromosome/position hypotheses exclude coexpr_k562 and that exclusion does NOT transfer: its justification was that aneuploid subclonal copy-number variation makes same-chromosome genes co-vary, supplying chromosome identity through DNA dosage. This label is derived from curated regulatory-network DIRECTION and has no chromosomal or dosage-linked component, so K562 aneuploidy gives it no privileged channel. esm2 is fair for the symmetric reason: the label is a property of a gene's upstream regulators, not of its own coding sequence, and all TFs (whose DNA-binding domains let esm2 win tf_role at 0.794) are excluded from the labelled set.
meta.measured: Verified by running this loader, not copied from the proposal. DoRothEA A/B/C unique edges 32,286; TRRUST rows 9,396; |E|=37,232; |TFS|=917 (643 DoRothEA sources + 795 TRRUST sources, overlapping); |TF->TF|=5,172; 601 TFs get an h; 3,207 genes labelled; 3,117 overlap the coexpr panel; 1,106 survive the 6-basis intersection. Label is near tie-free (3,063 distinct values over 3,207 genes), raw range [-0.719, +0.932]. PRE-RESIDUAL correlations on the 1,106: rho(label, log in-degree)=-0.234, rho(label, breadth)=-0.089, rho(label, abundance)=-0.101 — all three reproduce the pre-registered values.
meta.intersection_cost: coexpr_k562's 6,546-gene table is what binds the intersection: without it the five remaining bases share 2,968 of the labelled genes, with it 1,106. Admitting coexpr_k562 as a fair reference therefore costs 63% of the labelled genes. Stated here rather than silently paid — if the screen comes back marginal, the five-basis-without-k562 run at n=2,968 is the better-powered re-test, and coexpr_k562 should then be reported as a standalone matched adjudicator (the cc_phase_matched_ref pattern) rather than dropped.
meta.mandatory_extra_baseline: A margin measured only against screen.py's `coexpr` is inflated by construction — that basis is ~8x too weak. Before any margin here is admissible, re-score against the LSA-256 pooled-corpus shallow co-occurrence basis: shallow_coocc_baseline.lsa over coocc_fair.stream_binary across coocc_strongest.PANELS. This is the baseline that has repeatedly overturned apparent model wins in this program (cf. the raw-profile-vs-factorization retraction) and it is not part of screen.py's BASES.
meta.sensitivity: Leave-one-regulator-out over the top 5 contributors before promoting. Measured on the 1,106-gene scored intersection: 376 distinct regulators contribute, top 5 are ETS1 (254 genes), E2F4 (238), E2F1 (214), EGR1 (214), STAT1 (209). Drop each in turn from the h-carrying set, recompute the mean, re-screen; the margin must survive all five. NB on the full 3,207 the top contributors are different (CEBPA 651, STAT1 644, TFAP2C 597, HNF4A 583, FOS 573) — the top-5 list is intersection-specific because the 6-basis intersection is heavily reshaped by coexpr_k562's 6,546-gene table, so run the LORO check on whichever gene set the reported margin was actually computed over.
meta.causal_followup: Only if Gates 1-2 pass. Split labelled genes in half; on half A build the steering direction as the CENTROID DIFFERENCE between top-decile and bottom-decile depth genes — NOT a fitted probe vector, and never read back with a probe fitted on those directions (the tautology trap scores 1.000 for every basis including co-expression). Push +alpha*direction at one set of gene positions in a real cell trajectory and read the model's own next-gene logits at DISJOINT positions so the effect must travel through attention. Prediction: logit mass shifts toward held-out half-B high-depth genes, monotone in alpha, with a norm-matched random direction near zero and a sham direction from permuted labels near zero. Report against the real-token substitution ceiling, not as a raw delta (cf. steering-magnitude-deflation).

Fit and emitted on the 4-basis intersection (maxtoki_lmhead x maxtoki_we x coexpr x esm2) n=16,837, restricted to genes present in GO -> 16,412 labels. VERIFIED: raw mean 2.412 sd 0.842 range 0.00-5.30; residual sd 0.822; the design explains only 4.8% of raw variance and rho(raw, residual) = 0.969.
meta.unfair_reason: DELIBERATELY EMPTY — no reference is unfair for this hypothesis, and this is not an oversight. Do NOT copy h_chromosome's unfair_refs=['coexpr_k562'] block: that exemption rests on a specific physical mechanism (K562 is an aneuploid cancer line, so subclonal copy-number variation makes same-chromosome genes co-vary through DNA DOSAGE rather than co-regulation). DNA dosage has no route to a gene's LITERATURE ANNOTATION COUNT — aneuploidy changes how many copies of a gene a cell carries, not how many papers were written about it — so coexpr_k562 is a fully FAIR baseline here and must be beaten like the others. It does shrink the scored gene set to 6,265 (only 6,546 rows), which is a POWER cost, not a fairness problem; report that margin with its gene set stated. All four references (coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562, esm2) must clear MIN_MARGIN = 0.02.
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, leaning NEGATIVE, and informative either way. Honest priors, in order of likelihood: (1) ESM2 wins — well-studied genes are enriched for kinases/TFs/receptors, families ESM2 reads straight off the residues. This is the modal outcome (all five go_GO* hypotheses lost to ESM2) and if it happens the verdict is REJECT, reported as the family channel, NOT rationalised. (2) Nothing beats the co-expression panels, because after abundance and breadth are removed the remaining annotation signal is mostly noise (139 distinct raw values, sd 0.84). (3) The interesting outcome: MaxToki beats all four by > 0.02, which would mean the gene table carries a literature-popularity coordinate with no expression-level or sequence-family explanation — a study-bias axis inside a model that never saw a paper, most plausibly via training-corpus context diversity. Expect this row to track its un-residualised twin `annotation_richness` almost exactly (rho = 0.969); a large gap between the two would itself be a red flag worth chasing.

meta.source: Pseudo-partition of TOKEN-ID space over exactly h_chromosome's universe. symbol->token row via gm_lib's own idiom (gm_lib.py:110-126; MT_TOK token dict x ENSMAP ensembl->symbol, first occurrence) -> 20,271 symbols, matching the maxtoki_lmhead row count. Genes = autosomal genes in coords() that carry a token, sorted by token id -> n=18,287. The real 22-class chromosome size multiset (min 210, median 770, max 1988) is laid down as CONTIGUOUS token-ID blocks after a rigid rotation of int(frac*770) positions; chromosomes are ordered by median token position so block k inherits the size and approximate location of chromosome order[k]. Registered slot frac=0.50 (SHIFT=385); ladder 0.25/0.50/0.75 via labels_at(). MEASURED DIAGNOSTICS (diagnostics(), k=1 kNN on token_id alone, screen's own 5 folds, balanced acc): AMI(pseudo, real chromosome) = 0.0950 / 0.0984 / 0.0938 across the ladder — reproduces the spec. BUT THE SPEC'S MATCHING ASSUMPTION IS FALSE AS MEASURED: kNN(token_id) gives 0.998 for the pseudo label against 0.490 for the real chromosome (k=50: 0.374), not the asserted near-equality at ~0.49. Cause: the real chromosome is not a token block at all — 9,340 maximal runs over 18,287 genes, MEAN RUN LENGTH 2.0 GENES, adjacent-token same-chromosome 0.489 (reproducing RESULTS.md sec 12 exactly), whereas the construction lays down 22 runs. The pair is size- and scale-matched but the pseudo label is ~2x EASIER on the token-ID channel, so the comparison is one-sided (see expect). labels_matched(frac) ships the genuinely matched control built and measured here — the real label vector ROTATED along token-ID order, preserving run structure and class sizes exactly: kNN(token_id) = 0.485/0.484/0.485 (parity with the real 0.490) at AMI 0.0445/0.0379/0.0349 (LOWER than the block recipe, i.e. more orthogonal to the real chromosome). It dominates the registered recipe on both criteria and should take the next screen slot. labels_disagreement_subset() = the registered label on the 15,311/18,287 genes (83.7%) whose block disagrees with that block's majority chromosome (22 classes, min 167), bounding inherited signal. Universe check: the six-basis intersection is 6,307 genes, of which this label covers 6,133 — the same set h_chromosome is scored on, then subsampled to GENE_CAP=5000 under the same SEED, so the paired real-vs-pseudo comparison is exact.
meta.unfair_reason: None declared, and none is defensible — deliberately. Every reference sits at chance (~0.045 on 22 classes) by construction: a rotated partition of vocabulary-index space has no expression, sequence, or dosage correlate, so coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562 and esm2 are all fair and all must be run. In particular coexpr_k562 is GENUINELY FAIR here, unlike on h_chromosome/h_position: its CNV channel supplies chromosome identity through DNA dosage in an aneuploid line, which says nothing about vocabulary ORDER. That matters strategically — the chromosome and position rows survive only because coexpr_k562 is excluded, and a control aimed at those rows must not inherit the same concession. This row is therefore independent of the load-bearing exclusion. Declaring any ref unfair here would be the selective-baseline trap applied to the one row whose baseline margins are meaningless anyway.
meta.expect: GATE STRESS TEST, subtractive by design — NEVER promote this row to the ATLAS as a passer, whatever it scores. Prediction: large positive margin over all four references (none can express a vocabulary-index partition) and therefore a spurious 'decodable + model_specific' verdict. THE BASELINE MARGINS ON THIS ROW ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING; the decisive comparison is against h_chromosome's OWN 0.511 on the identical gene set, folds and metric. Pre-registered ONE-SIDED decision rule (one-sided because the measured kNN(token_id) asymmetry 0.998 vs 0.490 means this label is strictly easier on the confounded channel, not matched to it): (a) pseudo <= 0.15 -> chromosome is EXCULPATED against the strongest available token-ID alternative, and more strongly than the spec anticipated, since that alternative was handed a 2x advantage and still collapsed. (b) pseudo ~ 0.5 -> this does NOT license 'chromosome is token-block memorisation' — the confound is amplified, not controlled — and the only licensed reading is methodological: Gate 2 as written has no defence against model-internal index artefacts, so 'beats every reference' is not 'is biology', and every row whose verdict rests on baseline margins alone needs re-adjudicating. Either way, run labels_matched() next: it is the token-ID-matched, lower-AMI control that actually settles the original question. CAUSAL FOLLOW-UP only if Gates 1-2 pass, and there the causal test is the ALARM, not the finding: run the IDENTICAL Stage-3 harness used for chromosome_1b (per-block centroid-difference directions from the model table, push at one gene block, read MaxToki's own next-gene logits at a DISJOINT block, norm-matched random control, monotone alpha ladder, effect quoted against the substitution ceiling per memory steering-magnitude-deflation). If a semantically meaningless token-block direction steers comparably to the +0.169 / 22-of-22-positive result on the 1B model, the steering readout is measuring vocabulary neighbourhood rather than a computational variable, and the headline plus both Stage-3 results must be re-adjudicated.

meta.source: human/mouse conserved-synteny breakpoints from UCE species_chrom.csv, loaded WITHOUT the species=='human' filter. Orthologues = upper-cased symbol identity (16,244 shared; 15,626 after restricting human to autosomes 1-22 and mouse to autosomes 1-19; symbols verified unique within each species). Per human autosome, genes with a mouse orthologue are sorted by human start (mergesort on finite starts). A gene with >=3 neighbours on each side of a +-5-gene window is 'breakpoint' if the modal mouse chromosome of its 5 left neighbours differs from that of its 5 right neighbours, OR |median(mouse start, left 5) - median(mouse start, right 5)| > 10 Mb; else 'interior'. 15,494 scorable, 1,190 breakpoints (7.7%). The scored set is then MATCHED: restricted first to the six-basis common gene set (6,307 symbols; coexpr_k562 at 6,546 is the binding constraint), then within each (human chromosome x local-density quintile) stratum equal breakpoint and interior counts are kept, rng seed 0. Local density = log1p(#genes within +-1 Mb of the human start, focal excluded), computed on the FULL 18,916-gene human autosomal set and binned on that full distribution, never on the reduced common set. Final n=848 (424 per class) across 22 chromosomes.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE — deliberately empty, and this is the row's single most important property. The sibling `chromosome` and `position` hypotheses must exclude coexpr_k562 because K562 is aneuploid: subclonal copy-number variation makes same-chromosome genes co-vary, so those labels leak through DNA DOSAGE rather than co-regulation. That mechanism cannot reach this label. Copy number is a HUMAN dosage signal over multi-megabase segments; the label here is defined by MOUSE coordinates and is matched WITHIN human chromosome and within local density, so a uniform human segmental gain is constant across both classes by construction. K562 therefore enters as an ordinary, fair reference and is gated on, as are coexpr, coexpr_devel and esm2. All four references are fair. A k562 win would be evidence of a leak in the label construction that we have not identified, and must be investigated, not excused.

design_oracles.measured_on: all-gene matched set (same construction, no common-gene restriction), n=2378, 1189/class
design_oracles.protocol: LogisticRegression on standardised features, 5-fold StratifiedKFold(shuffle, seed 0), identical folds across the four oracles, out-of-fold ROC-AUC

registered_values.note: from the independent construction this hypothesis was registered with (n=2380, 67 strata). This file measures n=2378 / 82 strata; the first three oracles agree to ~0.02, the ceiling does not (0.626 vs 0.577). The scored set is n=848 under both.

design_oracles.floor_note: THE FLOOR IS NOT 0.500. Breakpoints remain non-uniformly distributed after chromosome x density matching, so a coordinate-only oracle reaches 0.626. A model basis must beat 0.626 — the conservative (higher) of this file's own measurement and the registered 0.577 — before anything is claimed. Between 0.500 and 0.626 the model has recovered nothing the human coordinate did not already give.

meta.scoring_note: Two requirements the default screen does not meet. (1) Enter each co-expression panel ADDITIONALLY in 128-dim SVD form (coexpr_fact.py; fact_coexpr_128.npz, fact_coexpr_devel_128.npz, fact_coexpr_k562_128.npz already exist in gm_lib.CACHE). The raw 2500-cell profile arm under-powers every reference and inflates every model margin — see memory `wrong-null-raw-profile-vs-factorization`, where factorising the same cells moved a baseline 0.044 -> 0.692 and retracted a model-specificity claim. A verdict resting on the raw-profile arm alone is not reportable. (2) Compare the model score against design_oracles['honest_floor'], not against 0.500 and not only against the permutation null: the permutation null IS ~0.500 here and passing it is necessary, not sufficient.
meta.gated_bases: maxtoki_lmhead, maxtoki_we vs coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562, esm2 — all four references fair, none excluded. EXPLORATORY AND NOT GATED (reporting the max over them would manufacture a winner): scgpt_we, geneformer_we, ctx_L00..ctx_L11 and the cell-type-conditioned ctx variants. Report those descriptively, flagged as exploratory.
meta.group_by_note: Deliberately NO group_by. Matching equalises the chromosome distribution across classes exactly, so chromosome carries no marginal signal (one-hot oracle 0.410, below chance); grouping would only shatter n=848 into 22 pieces of ~39.
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, and informative either way — this is the hardest genome label in the program and the first whose ground truth lives in a species no basis has seen. PASS (model > 0.626, beating all four references) would mean the table carries ancestral chromosomal-domain structure that must have been inferred from human co-occurrence alone, and it would be the first genome result that does NOT depend on the coexpr_k562 exclusion — which is exactly the objection the chromosome and position findings currently carry. FAIL would cleanly bound the genome channel to human-coordinate-shaped quantities. Prior leans slightly negative: 424 positives is modest power for a subtle boundary effect, and the honest floor is high.

meta.source: DoRothEA A/B/C (D tier dropped: it is the bulk-co-expression-inferred tier, 244,276 of 276,562 edges) + UCE species_chrom coordinates. Universe = autosomal genes with >=1 A/B/C regulator (8,901). Per chromosome, universe members sorted by true bp start; for gene g at sorted index i the neighbours are the 5 preceding + 5 following universe members (exactly 10 required, else the gene is dropped). raw(g) = fraction of those 10 neighbours h with T(g) & T(h) non-empty. Residualised by least squares on D=[1, F, F**2] where F is the z-scored [log1p(#regulators of g), mean over neighbours of log1p(#regulators of h), fractional chromosome position start/max_start, log1p(bp span of the 10-neighbour window)]. n=8,681; raw mean 0.171 sd 0.186; removes 47.7% of variance; residual sd 0.134; largest tie block 1.
meta.scoring_note: MEASURED common-gene-set sizes, which contradict the spec's pre-registered '~8,600': the SIX-basis common set (with coexpr_k562) intersects this label at n=3,409; the FIVE-basis set (without it) at n=7,994. coexpr_k562 is the binding constraint — the Replogle panel has only 6,546 symbols and covers 3,411 of the 8,681 labelled genes. Keeping k562 in the gate is CORRECT here (see unfair_reason) but costs 61% of the label. Report BOTH: the strict four-reference gate on n=3,409 and the higher-powered three-reference read on n=7,994, and quote n with every number. The smaller n is a coverage limit, NOT a k562 exclusion, and must not be reported as one.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE — deliberately empty, and this includes coexpr_k562, which the sibling `chromosome` and `position` hypotheses DO exclude. Their exclusion rests on copy-number dosage: in an aneuploid line whole arms are amplified, so same-arm genes co-vary and chromosome IDENTITY plus COARSE POSITION leak through DNA dosage. That mechanism does not transfer here. Whole-arm dosage is a megabase-uniform multiplier: it lifts a gene and all ten of its immediate neighbours (a window whose median span is far below arm scale) by the SAME factor, so it cannot manufacture a contrast between neighbours that share g's regulators and neighbours that do not. It is also exactly the component the residualisation removes — fractional chromosome position and local window span are both IN the design matrix. So all four references are fair and all four must be beaten by >0.02. If coexpr_k562 nonetheless WINS, that is an INFORMATIVE NEGATIVE pointing at megabase dosage-domain structure (i.e. the label is picking up CNV-block boundaries rather than co-regulation) and it must be REPORTED AS SUCH, not re-excluded post hoc. Requested as an addition, not an exclusion: a 128-dim SVD factorisation arm for each coexpr panel, since a raw expression profile is not a co-expression baseline (see memory wrong-null-raw-profile-vs-factorization).
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, informative in both directions. The label is the INTERSECTION of a regulatory relation (shared TFs) and a positional relation (chromosomal adjacency); the model is the only basis in the panel that could hold both at once, since correlation carries no coordinate and sequence carries neither. A pass says the gene table encodes domain-level regulatory coherence beyond local density, regulator count and position — and licenses the near-vs-far steering readout, which is unusually well controlled because the generic co-expression push cancels by design. A clean fail is also worth having: the expression-side twin (nb_coexpr_domain) was not decodable (z=1.3), so a null here would say the co-regulatory-block channel is simply absent rather than merely redundant with co-expression. Watch coexpr_k562 specifically — see unfair_reason.

meta.source: DoRothEA A/B/C edges DEGREE-PRESERVING REWIRED, then the coreg_domain_share_resid pipeline re-run verbatim. Edge set is the real row's: keep iff the ';'-split confidence field intersects {A,B,C} (so the 14 'A;D'/'B;D'/'C;D' rows are in), 32286 unique (TF, target) pairs. Rewiring: 10*|E| = 322860 proposed double-edge swaps under numpy default_rng(0) over the sorted edge list; propose (a.tf, b.target) + (b.tf, a.target), reject duplicates and same-TF draws; 245250 accepted. Every TF out-degree and every target in-degree asserted invariant, |E| unchanged. tfsets are rebuilt from the rewired graph; the universe (autosomal genes with >=1 regulator), the coordinate sort, the K=10 annotated-neighbour windows, the four nuisance covariates and the least-squares residualisation on D=[1, Z, Z**2] are then IDENTICAL to the real row — the nuisance design matrix is bit-identical (asserted max |F_real - F_rewired| = 0). n = 8681, universe asserted identical to the real row's; raw mean share 0.140 sd 0.169 (real 0.171/0.186); residual sd 0.108, variance removed 0.592 (real 0.134 / 0.477); largest tie block 1, so no tie-reinjection degeneracy. Exposes labels_real() and raw_share(rewired=) so both arms can be built from this one file, and _audit reproduces the real row's published numbers exactly through this mirror. NB the pre-registered spec quoted |E| = 32272 and 245076 accepted swaps, which is the EXACT-MATCH confidence filter; the real row as implemented uses the ';'-split filter, and this file follows the IMPLEMENTED real row so the degree columns match it. That choice is what makes n = 8681 rather than 8680.
meta.pairing_note: THIS ROW IS ONLY INTERPRETABLE AS A DIFFERENCE. It must be scored on the SAME gene set, SAME folds, SAME metric and SAME reference set as coreg_domain_share_resid, in the SAME cycle. Gene-set identity is guaranteed and asserted on this side: in-degree preservation makes the universe and the K=10 windows identical, so both arms return the same 8681 symbols in the same order. Inherit the real row's coverage caveat verbatim: the six-basis common set (with coexpr_k562) intersects this label at n=3409 and the five-basis set at n=7994, because the Replogle panel carries only 6546 symbols. Quote n with every number, and apply the SAME common-gene-set choice to both arms — differencing a margin measured on n=3409 against one measured on n=7994 would be meaningless.
meta.decision_rule: Pre-registered before running. If the rewired row lands within MIN_MARGIN = 0.02 of the real row on BOTH z AND the model/reference margin, coreg_domain_share_resid is WITHDRAWN — pulled from the ATLAS, not caveated — and the outcome recorded in PROGRAM.md's calibration table. If the rewired row collapses toward zero while the real row holds, the co-regulation claim is cleared against the correct null and earns its Stage-2 steering test. This row must NEVER itself be promoted to Stage 3.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE, and none is defensible here — the decisive statistic is a DIFFERENCE of margins between two rows, so any reference dropped from this arm must also be dropped from the real arm or the subtraction is invalid, and dropping it from both only shrinks the evidence base. The four references (coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562, esm2) plus the SVD arm therefore all stay in, matching the real row's own empty unfair_refs. In particular coexpr_k562 is NOT excused by the CNV/dosage argument the chromosome and position rows invoke: whole-arm copy-number gain is a megabase-uniform multiplier that lifts a gene and all ten of its immediate neighbours by the same factor, so it cannot manufacture a contrast between neighbours that share regulators and neighbours that do not — and it contributes that channel IDENTICALLY to both arms, so it cancels exactly in the differenced statistic. Excluding it would be the selective-baseline trap applied to the one row whose absolute baseline margins are uninformative by design.
meta.expect: EXPECTED TO FAIL, and subtractive by design — this is a CONTROL, not a candidate discovery. Prediction under the co-regulation hypothesis: the rewired field scores near zero and far below coreg_domain_share_resid, because the swapped TF->target pairs never existed in any cell and nothing in the training corpus could encode them. Prediction under the nuisance hypothesis: the rewired field tracks the real one closely, because the model is reading the annotation's degree sequence and genomic spacing — a citation-bias field, since well-studied genes have more annotated regulators and cluster in well-studied loci — rather than regulation. That nuisance channel is not hypothetical: the real row's own audit reports raw rho = +0.541 against own regulator count, so the degree signal DOMINATES the raw label and the whole claim rests on the quadratic residualisation having removed it cleanly. THIS ROW'S OWN BASELINE MARGINS ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING; a 'decodable + model_specific' verdict here is a kill order for its sibling, not a finding. NOTE the measured rho(real_resid, rewired_resid) = +0.062: after residualisation the arms are near-independent, which is what a matched null should look like — they share their whole nuisance structure and almost nothing else. The small positive coupling that remains biases this row TOWARD firing, i.e. toward withdrawal: conservative in the right direction, since a gate-blocker that erred toward silence would be the dangerous one.

meta.source: Geneformer gene_median_dictionary_gc104M.pkl (42,005 ensembl -> non-zero median expression over the pretraining corpus; md5 caedb1ca9c6921024b0b378dd05b1686, byte-identical to the copy MaxToki's own adapter loads at maxtoki_adapter.py:30,77-81 and divides by at line 140). Mapped to UPPERCASE symbols by inverting gene_name_id_dict_gc104M.pkl (first occurrence per ensembl, the gm_lib._maxtoki idiom) and restricted to the 20,271 ENSG entries of MaxToki's token_dictionary.json, so the label covers only tokens the model actually has. Label = rank(log median) minus its OLS fit on [1, rank(coexpr mean abundance), rank(coexpr breadth)], rank-based because the screen scores continuous targets with Spearman. FIT AND EMITTED ON THE 6-BASIS SCORED INTERSECTION (n=6,307), NOT on the wider coexpr overlap — see the SCORED-SET CORRECTION in the module docstring, this is load-bearing. VERIFIED on the emitted set: residual is exactly Pearson-orthogonal to both rank regressors (~4e-15) and Spearman rho(residual, abundance) = 0.117, rho(residual, breadth) = 0.116; the design absorbs R^2 = 0.679 of the raw rank variance there. Contamination check (brief step 7), measured ON THE EMITTED LABEL: rho(residual, nb_gene_density) = +0.120 over the 6,133 shared genes, well below the |rho| > 0.3 threshold (the wider pre-correction fit gave -0.059 over 16,232 genes; quote the +0.120, it is the one that describes what gets scored). NB the brief's quoted n=26,628 / rho 0.562 / 0.543 are NOT reproducible under its own step 3 and should not be quoted; the token-restricted values are 17,359 / 0.452 / 0.416.
meta.unfair_reason: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and for this hypothesis that is a VIRTUE rather than a concession. Do NOT copy h_chromosome's unfair_refs=['coexpr_k562']: that exemption rests on aneuploid copy-number dosage making same-chromosome genes co-vary, a mechanism specific to a positional label. Copy number has no privileged route to a constant computed as the non-zero median over a DIFFERENT corpus (Geneformer's 104M-cell pretraining set, not K562). coexpr_k562 is the most informative baseline here precisely because it is a different cell line: if K562 expression recovers the corpus-median residual, the 'corpus-specific normalisation' story is dead on the spot. This row is therefore INDEPENDENT of the k562 exclusion currently propping up the chromosome and position rows, and needs no exemption of its own. All four standing references (coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562, esm2) are fair and must clear MIN_MARGIN = 0.02. The honest cost of taking no exemption is stated in the docstring: coexpr_k562 gates the scored set down to 6,307 genes, which is a POWER cost, not a fairness problem.
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, and informative in every direction — but NOT INTERPRETABLE FROM THE STANDING BASES ALONE. The verdict is a DISSOCIATION between two references that are not in screen.py's BASES and that this loader is barred from adding: geneformer_we (identical vocabulary and identical median dictionary — positive control) and scgpt_we (different vocabulary, bins HVGs, never touches this dictionary — negative control). MaxToki high + geneformer_we high + scgpt_we low => the effect is tokenizer-induced and the claim stands. scgpt_we equally high => the label is expression-driven, the tokenizer story dies, and a large MaxToki-over-coexpr margin does NOT rescue it. Ranked priors: (1) the residual is largely corpus-vs-panel measurement noise and nothing beats the co-expression panels; (2) the interesting outcome, MaxToki and geneformer_we decode it while scgpt_we does not, which would mean the gene table carries the tokenizer's own normalisation constant — a genuinely model-internal quantity with no expression-level explanation left; (3) ESM2 wins, which would mean the corpus median is tracking sequence-recognisable gene families and the verdict is REJECT, reported as the family channel and not rationalised. Read strictly alongside its companion corpus_median_raw: coexpr is EXPECTED to win that raw row, and if it does not, this residualised row is uninterpretable and the raw-profile coexpr arm is under-powered — re-run both against the 128-dim SVD factorisation before quoting anything.

meta.source: Cross-model kNN placement consistency. Universe = symbols(scgpt_we) INTERSECT symbols(geneformer_we) INTERSECT symbols(maxtoki_lmhead), n=19153 VERIFIED. For scgpt_we and geneformer_we SEPARATELY: restrict rows to the universe, mean-centre columns, L2-normalise rows, cosine kNN K=100 excluding self. J(g) = |N_scgpt INTERSECT N_gf| / |N_scgpt UNION N_gf|. Full-universe J: mean 0.0485 sd 0.0709 q10 0.0050 q50 0.0204 q90 0.1299, 5.06% zeros; random baseline K^2/N/(2K - K^2/N) = 0.00262, so mean ~18.5x chance. LABEL = J residualised in RANK SPACE on [expr_breadth, log1p(expr_abundance)] from the coexpr panel via [vander(u,4), vander(w,4)[:,:3]]; residual retains rho +0.889 with raw J and carries |rho| <= 0.013 with both covariates (plain OLS left 0.31-0.35 and was rejected — see docstring). Emitted on the 16803 universe genes that also have a coexpr panel row. Every number: Spearman rho, 19,153-gene universe, K=100.
meta.provenance: CRITICAL: maxtoki_lmhead is the PROBED basis and defines the universe ONLY. It never enters the label. The label is computed from scgpt_we and geneformer_we alone. Neither maxtoki table, nor any contextual ctx_* basis, nor any expression panel contributes to J; the panel enters only as the two nuisance covariates that are REMOVED.
meta.cv_note: Random folds, NOT grouped CV. This label is not positional and has no chromosome, locus or family scoping, so a group split would remove variance the hypothesis is about. Pair with a label-shuffle null (screen.py's permutation null is exactly this).
meta.raw_variant: raw_labels() in this module returns un-residualised J on the same genes. The brief requires BOTH be reported. 3000-gene preview (maxtoki_lmhead / coexpr / esm2 / coexpr_svd128): raw 0.622 / 0.398 / 0.317 / 0.354; residual 0.547 / 0.230 / 0.205 / 0.222. Residualising costs the model 0.075 and coexpr 0.168 — a large raw/resid gap on the BASELINE is the abundance story, and it is shown rather than hidden. Registering the raw arm needs a sibling auto_hyp file this agent may not write (one file per hypothesis).
meta.factorisation_check: MANDATED 128-dim SVD factorisation of the coexpr arm was RUN and INVERTS for this label: SVD makes coexpr WEAKER (raw J 0.398 -> 0.354; residual 0.230 -> 0.222), unlike chromosome/coexpr_devel where results/coexpr_fact.json shows 0.042 -> 0.585. The raw 7500-dim profile screen.py already feeds is the STRONGER co-expression arm here, so screen.py's default is conservative for this label and the margin does not depend on adding the factorisation. Mandate still stands for positional labels.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE — deliberately empty, and this label explicitly DOES NOT INHERIT the coexpr_k562 exclusion carried by h_chromosome and h_position. Their justification is DNA DOSAGE: in an aneuploid line whole segments are amplified, so same-segment genes co-vary and CHROMOSOME identity leaks into the panel through copy number. That argument has zero purchase here. This label is not positional — it is a kNN-agreement statistic between two model embedding tables — and no copy-number mechanism supplies cross-model neighbourhood overlap. Copy-number gain shifts a gene's mean level, which is precisely the abundance channel the residualisation already removes. So coexpr_k562 stays fully IN the gate alongside coexpr, coexpr_devel and esm2: all four are FAIR and all four must be beaten by MIN_MARGIN=0.02. A k562 win here would be a RED FLAG about the label, not a nuisance to excuse.
meta.expect: POSITIVE and, if it holds, the batch's most interesting result — it would decompose a published NEGATIVE (H24/H17/H20: models do not agree on gene placement) into a real per-gene variable that a third model encodes. 3000-gene preview supports it: maxtoki_lmhead 0.547 vs coexpr 0.230 / esm2 0.205 / coexpr_svd128 0.222, margin ~0.32 against MIN_MARGIN 0.02. Not yet screened against coexpr_devel or coexpr_k562. INFORMATIVE IF IT FAILS TOO: an esm2 win would say cross-model consistency is just gene-family membership; a coexpr win would say it is just co-expression sharpness that the abundance residualisation failed to catch. RESIDUAL RISK: all three models are transformers on scRNA corpora, so a win means 'shared across SCFMs', NOT 'MaxToki-specific'.

meta.source: Raw MaxToki token-ID (embedding/unembedding row). symbol->token row via gm_lib's own idiom (gm_lib.py:110-126): MT_TOK (ensembl id -> token row, JSON) x ENSMAP (gene_name_id_dict, symbol -> ensembl, pickle), row<vocab(20275) filter, argsort + np.unique first-occurrence. VERIFIED byte-exact against G.basis('maxtoki_lmhead'): 20,271 symbols, ZERO row-vector mismatches, so the label IS the row the maxtoki_lmhead/maxtoki_we bases decode. label = float(token_row); kind=continuous, no group_by (this is a genome-WIDE index, not a within-chromosome coordinate); label-permutation null, the screen's KFold ridge. MEASURED DIAGNOSTICS (diagnostics(), 5-fold ridge, abs Spearman, per-basis common set, cap 4000): maxtoki_lmhead 0.499, maxtoki_we 0.467; geneformer_we 0.471 (UNFAIR, shared tokenizer); scgpt_we 0.353, esm2 0.343, coexpr 0.260, coexpr_devel 0.158, coexpr_k562 0.143. The spec predicted every reference at ~0; MEASUREMENT REFUTES THAT — the token-ID is assigned in Ensembl-accession order, which runs in chromosome/position-correlated blocks, so the raw token-ID is a monotone GENOMIC-RANK proxy that every genome-position-aware basis reads (chromosome eta^2 = 0.0254; within-chromosome mean |Spearman(token_id, start)| = 0.067). scgpt_we's 0.353 on a DISJOINT vocabulary is the proof: it cannot share an index, so the channel is genome position, not a shared row number. Sibling control to chrom_tokenblock_shifted (that one stress-tests the categorical chromosome gate with a pseudo-partition; this one stress-tests the continuous gate with the bare index).
meta.unfair_reason: Geneformer shares MaxToki's exact tokenizer (20,274/20,275 identical ensembl->row mappings, same lab; gm_lib.py:54-58), so a gene lands on the SAME token-ID row in both tables. Decoding MaxToki's token-ID from Geneformer's embeddings (measured 0.471) is therefore decoding Geneformer's OWN row index — the identical arbitrary bookkeeping channel, carried by a shared vocabulary construction, not by independent biology. Used as a cross-model REPLICATION basis it would falsely certify the token-ID signal as generalising across models when it is one tokenizer counted twice; that is the mechanism that makes it unfair. (NB the screen's REF_BASES do not include geneformer_we, so this declaration is a forward-looking guard for any cross-model use, not a live gate exclusion — and it is the anti-selective direction: geneformer would PASS, and it is declared unfair to prevent an inflated generalisation claim, never to rescue the hypothesis.) The four screen references (coexpr, coexpr_devel, coexpr_k562, esm2) are ALL FAIR and are all scored; scgpt_we is FAIR too (disjoint vocab). The spurious Gate-2 pass over those fair references is exactly the point of the row.
meta.expect: EXPECTED PASS, BY DESIGN MEANINGLESS — the calibration control the ATLAS lacked. Prediction: decodable (maxtoki ~0.50, z enormous vs the label-permutation null) AND model_specific (beats the hardest fair reference esm2 0.343 by margin +0.156 > MIN_MARGIN). Both gates pass. THE PASS IS NOT A FINDING: it proves 'decodable + beats expression + beats sequence' is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT — the model's own vocabulary index clears both gates. NEVER promote this row to the ATLAS whatever it scores. MEASURED CORRECTION carried in META['source']: the references are NOT at ~0 as the spec assumed; the token-ID is a genome-position proxy (scgpt_we 0.353 on a disjoint vocab proves the channel is genome position, not a shared index). The lesson survives and sharpens: a label that is decodable-from-the-model AND truly content-free cannot exist, because whatever the table encodes about its row order is structured (here, genome order). CAUSAL FOLLOW-UP — this is the pre-registered Gate-3 NEGATIVE control for the chromosome headline, and here the negative is the finding. Build the token-ID centroid direction from the model table, push it at one set of gene positions, read MaxToki's OWN next-gene logits at DISJOINT positions, norm-matched random control, monotone alpha ladder, effect quoted against the substitution ceiling (memory steering-magnitude-deflation). PREDICTION: no coherent logit shift and no chromosome-enrichment shift. IF token-ID steering DOES move logits by ~+0.05, that is a RED ALERT that chromosome's +0.055 is not chromosome-specific but a generic vocabulary-neighbourhood / genome-order effect, and the headline plus both Stage-3 steering results must be re-adjudicated.

meta.source: local compartment TEXTURE from UCE species_chrom coordinates. For each autosomal gene at coordinate-sorted index i: d1 = log1p(#gene starts in [start-1Mb, start+1Mb], self excluded); the TEXTURE label = std of d1 over all genes whose start is within +-5 Mb of gene i (self included, require >= 5 genes in the window else the gene is dropped), a contiguous slice under the coordinate sort so it is computed by cumulative-sum. LABEL = texture least-squares residualised WITHIN CHROMOSOME on [vander(position_rank, 6), d1, d1^2, rank(d1)] so the position channel and the local-density LEVEL channel (both already won) are removed, leaving a second-moment (variance-of-density) statistic. Chromosomes whose residual still exceeds |Spearman| 0.15 vs position OR vs d1 are DROPPED. Verified feasibility: n~18911 before the audit drop; residual |rho| vs position 0.027 mean / 0.086 max, vs d1 0.034 mean / 0.116 max; residual sd ~0.10. Distinct from the FAILED density_asymmetry_resid (signed gradient): residual corr with signed asymmetry only +0.038.
meta.model_specificity_rule: scgpt_we and geneformer_we are FAIR baselines in the gate; report maxtoki minus each. MaxToki-specific ONLY on a > 0.02 margin over BOTH. Otherwise reframe as an SCFM-GENERAL compartment-texture channel, not a MaxToki idiosyncrasy.
meta.unfair_reason: NONE — deliberately empty, coexpr_k562 INCLUDED. The sibling chromosome/position hypotheses exclude k562 because whole-chromosome aneuploidy amplifies an entire chromosome, so same-chromosome genes co-vary through DNA DOSAGE and CHROMOSOME identity leaks. That excuse does NOT transfer to this label: (a) a uniform whole-chromosome dosage gain is a within-chromosome CONSTANT, absorbed by the per-chromosome residualisation intercept (vander(rank,6) carries the constant column); and (b) the label is a +-5 Mb VARIANCE of neighbour density counts, and a spatially uniform dosage adds the same offset everywhere in the window, leaving its dispersion unchanged — it cannot manufacture texture. So k562 stays IN the gate: a clean pass over it is positive evidence of chromatin-compartment structure rather than CNV dosage, and a k562 WIN here would be a RED FLAG about the label construction (an unidentified leak), not a nuisance to excuse.
meta.expect: UNCERTAIN, informative either way — a strictly harder ask than the +-1 Mb density-LEVEL family because it is a SECOND-MOMENT statistic. If it beats all fair baselines (with the > 0.02 SCFM margin), MaxToki carries a compartment-TEXTURE channel (interior-vs-edge homogeneity) separable from both position and the local density level it already won. If it collapses while nb_gene_density_resid passes, the model's density code carries the LEVEL but not its local dispersion — a clean negative, since the hard self-audit removes the 'position/d1 in disguise' escape hatch and the +0.038 correlation with signed asymmetry rules out a gradient re-detection.
